title: Spike: differential dataflow for structured reasoning
description:
Evaluate differential dataflow as Sutra's structured reasoning backbone. Port deps, impact, and co-change analyses into differential dataflow computations. Test incremental update latency, architectural constraints as maintained views, and temporal queries.

Key question: can differential dataflow replace Sutra's ad-hoc graph analyses with a unified, automatically incremental, temporally aware reasoning engine?

acceptance_criteria.text: 3 core analyses ported and producing identical results to current impl
Incremental update < 100ms for single-file change on 1K-function codebase
At least 2 architectural constraints expressed as maintained views
LOC comparison and ergonomics assessment written
Written verdict: viable / viable with caveats / not viable

implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Scaffolding — dd deps, spike binary, input collections from SQLite
Phase 2: Deps in DD — BFS reachability via iterate
Phase 3: Impact in DD — symbol-level transitive closure
Phase 4: Co-change in DD — self-join on commit
Phase 5: Incremental update benchmark (<100ms target)
Phase 6: Architectural constraints as maintained views (>=2)
Phase 7: Temporal query demo
Phase 8: Pagerank in DD
Phase 9: Write-up and verdict

Test codebases: sutra itself (~955 symbols), redox-kernel, linux/kernel
execution_record:
Verdict: viable with caveats.

3/3 analyses ported (deps exact match, impact superset, co-change 69/69 match).
Incremental: 19us simple views, 59us transitive reachability (well under 100ms).
2 constraints: cycle detection (49 files in cycles), forbidden deps.
Temporal: demonstrated multi-epoch fan-in queries.
PageRank: doesn't fit DD's monotone iterate — keep current impl.

Recommendation: use DD for maintained views (cycles, constraints, rollups),
keep imperative code for one-shot parameterized queries.
